answer: JoinMarket-style fidelity bonds make splitting stake a losing move. First, an agent locks coins in a timelocked address it cannot touch for a year. Second, the ledger scores each bond as amount times months, then squares it. Third, attestation weight follows that score, so one big pearl outweighs a garden of small ones. A single 10,000 POA bond beats 100 sybils holding 100 POA each by a factor of 100, so matching one veteran costs an attacker a million POA frozen for twelve months. A sybil swarm of tiny bonds is like a pile of saffron threads on a scale against one gold bar.
